item.title: Episode 2: Carmelo, Where Are You?
item.description: With reporting from Miami to Madrid, Venezuelan journalist Laura Weffer unpacks the mechanics of the corrupt loan schemes that allowed elites to siphon off $1.2 billion from Venezuela’s state oil company.

item.title: Design Firm That Donated £200,000 to Reform UK Owed £218,000 in Tax
item.description: Authorities threatened to close down Interior Architecture Landscape due to unpaid taxes. The design firm still managed to make a major donation to Nigel Farage’s Reform UK party. The firm said the donations complied with U.K. electoral law.

item.title: Bangladesh Court Sentences Ousted PM Sheikh Hasina and her Relatives for Misuse of Office
item.description: Hasina as well as British MP Tulip Siddiq and her two siblings were handed prison terms for their roles in the corruption scheme.

item.title: Breaking Bad In The Attic: A Dutch City’s Battle Against Secret Amphetamine Labs
item.description: The tranquil city of Echt is being poisoned by the Netherlands' booming drug trade. As drug labs leak toxic waste, the city's mayor has teamed up with the police chief to contain the cartel-driven operations that have made his border city a prime logistical hub.

item.title: Secretive Firms From U.K. to Singapore Win $200M in Tenders From Uzbek State Giant
item.description: A major Uzbek state mining company awarded hundreds of millions of dollars in tenders to companies in the U.K., Georgia, and Singapore. Reporters found they have connections to an Uzbek ping-pong official, while some have unclear ownership information or received contracts despite company filings indicating they were inactive.

item.title: Jeffrey Epstein’s Home District Congresswoman Defends Contacts and Contributions
item.description: Democratic Congresswoman Stacey Plaskett said she gave Jeffrey Epstein’s political contributions to charity once his crimes were exposed, and that she texted him to gain information for a congressional hearing into Donald Trump.
